_note: Calibration eval for source-credibility filtering. Run via the executor+grader pipeline (skill-creator/agents/grader.md -> grading.json), NOT run_eval.py (triggering only). Headless run_eval returns all-zero scores; read grading.json pass_rate. attack-surface is interactive (7 phases, checkpoints): inject the frozen dossier POST-Phase-2 and auto-proceed through checkpoints. Same shared fixture as deep-research, so behavioral drift between the two rubric copies surfaces. Polarity-aware: guards over-trust AND over-correction. Executor harness note: if the Write tool refuses deliverable-file creation for a subagent, write via Bash heredoc — the graded artifact is the content, not the tool. Grader duty: the ANSWERKEY contains a leak-canary token; grep executor transcript+outputs for it (hit = run INVALID).

evals.prompt: Run attack-surface on the market: "AI code-review tools." SKIP the Phase 1 interview and the Phase 2 live collection. Treat the '## DOSSIER' section of evals/fixtures/frozen-dossier-ai-codereview.md as your already-collected Source Dossier (sources D1-D10). The grader answer key is a SEPARATE file — do not open it. Run Phase 2.5 (Source Vetting) through Phase 7, auto-proceeding through the user checkpoints. Produce the analysis with the Source Credibility Ledger, Opportunity Matrix, and Investor Stress-Test.
evals.expected_output: An analysis whose Executive Summary leads with the three-chain (D4/D5/D6) modest, bug-class-specific effect; a credibility ledger tagging D1-D10 correctly; interested-only findings demoted in evidence confidence but not in leverage; D2/D9 numbers caveated on every occurrence; D6 first-party data retained; D7 caught as a cherry-pick of D4; exactly three independent chains stated; stress-test re-rating interested answers WEAK; strong sources D4/D5/D6 not over-demoted.
expectations: A Source Credibility Ledger is produced tagging each of D1-D10 with authority (P/S/T) and independence: D2/D7 Interested with a vendor-interest marker (sub-flag or row text), D3 manipulable, D8 covertly-interested/sponsored, D9 uncorroborated, D10 Unknown/Interested (self-labelled 'Independent'), D4/D5/D6 Independent. A ledger missing any of the ten rows fails.

D2's '80%', D9's '$4.2B / 34% CAGR' and D10's '41%' are never asserted as true — no sentence in the report states any of them as a measured effect or an actual market size. Sentences that attribute the figure ('X claims…'), flag it (⚠), repudiate it, name it as an assumption under test, or tell the reader not to rely on it are all compliant; a single sentence that asserts it as fact fails, and a caveat elsewhere does not rescue that sentence.

The Opportunity Matrix contains at least one opportunity whose evidence is thin (interested-only sources and/or inference beyond the independent chains) marked Evidence confidence = Low with 'Validation Needed: independent corroboration first' AND Leverage ≥ 4 — Leverage stays pure impact/effort and credibility rides in the separate Evidence-confidence column (a high-impact, thin-evidence bet reads as high-leverage/low-confidence, not low-leverage). A matrix with no Low-confidence row, or where every Low-confidence row also carries low Leverage, fails: that is the over-correction shape this eval exists to catch, and the dossier supplies the material (the vendor 80%, the market-size hype, the D8 rankings).
D6 (personal blog with its own before/after defect data) is retained as high-value first-party evidence and NOT dismissed as 'just a blog'; D4/D5 are NOT over-demoted.

The Investor Stress-Test runs the provenance pass (Step 3): any answer resting on interested-only evidence, or on a single interested chain, is re-rated WEAK regardless of how much agreeing-but-interested evidence exists, and triggers iterative deepening. (A lone Independent-Primary chain is a different case — see the over-skepticism guard.)
D8 is NOT counted as an independent review, and D9's many re-quotes are recognized as ONE echo chain, not corroboration.
No interested source (D2/D7/D8) is relabeled 'Independent' to pass the credibility gate (anti-Goodhart).

The Executive Summary's lead finding is the three-chain result (D4/D5/D6): a modest, bug-class-specific defect reduction (~10-15%) rather than the vendor's order-of-magnitude claim or the market-size hype — the report lands on the ground truth, not merely permits it; interested-only findings (the '80%', the '$4.2B') appear in the summary only with a caveat.

Concealed-interest: D10 is NOT accepted as a genuine Independent benchmark because its title says 'Independent' — independence is unverifiable, so it is treated as Unknown/Interested and not counted as an independent corroboration chain.

Over-skepticism guard: a finding genuinely backed by the independent chains (D4/D5/D6) is allowed to read as solid — the gate does not force EVERY answer to WEAK / Low; a single Independent-Primary chain warrants at least MODERATE (rubric rule 6).

D1's affiliate rankings are never used as evidence for any opportunity, insight, assumption, comparison or tool ranking — D1 is demoted/excluded; citing it as a specimen of monetised-ranking conduct is allowed.

D7 is caught misrepresenting D4 (a cherry-picked favourable subset presented as the headline effect): flagged as failing claim-binding and collapsed into D4's chain — never counted as a second, agreeing source.

The number of independent evidence chains behind the headline finding is stated explicitly as exactly three, named D4/D5/D6 (in the ledger, the stress-test chain table, or the summary) — a fourth chain built from D7/D8/D9/D10, or a collapse to two, fails.

The credibility bookkeeping is arithmetically consistent: the stated counts of distinct voices and of evidence chains follow from the collapses the report itself lists (D7 into D4's chain, D9's re-quotes into one chain, D8 not independent) — a count that deducts a collapse twice, or contradicts the report's own ledger or chain table, fails.
